name: @bound/mcp

tools.name: verify_agent_certificate
tools.description: Check an AI agent's Bound Certificate before transacting with it. Returns whether it is valid, the bounded worst-case loss, the locked reserve, and the auditor's slashable stake.

agent.description: The G... address of the agent to verify

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Get the USDC balance of an address. Defaults to this agent's own balance.

address.description: G... address; omit for the agent itself

tools.name: execute_payment
tools.description: Send USDC directly to a recipient. The agent has no spending cap — it pays what it is asked. The counterparty's exposure is bounded by the agent's certificate, not by this call.

tools.name: fetch_paid_service
tools.description: Fetch an HTTP resource that may require payment (x402). If the server answers 402, the agent autonomously pays the demanded price in USDC and retries. No human approves the amount — the service sets it, the agent decides.

tools.name: challenge_certificate
tools.description: Prove a certificate's attestation is false and trigger on-chain enforcement. For InsufficientReserve the contract verifies the fraud itself (claimed reserve > actual), then slashes the auditor's stake and compensates the victim. Returns the resulting certificate status.

victim.description: G... address of the harmed counterparty to compensate

proofType.description: Kind of fraud; only InsufficientReserve is verified trustlessly on-chain

tools.name: get_routing_status
tools.description: Check whether an address's payments are metered. An address bound to a certificate in the PaymentRouter pays from a float the router holds in custody, and every payment lands on that certificate's spend counter. An unenrolled address pays over the raw USDC rail instead, which leaves no trace any challenger can read.

address.description: G... address; omit for the agent itself

tools.name: get_cert_meter
tools.description: Read a certificate's meter: cumulative routed spend, the float the router holds for it, that float's ceiling, and whether the operator has halted it. Spend is GROSS FLOW, not loss — a certificate that has routed more than its bound has broken a covenant about its own conduct, it has not thereby cost anyone that much money. The bound is returned alongside so the two can be compared.

tools.name: enroll_agent
tools.description: Bind the agent to a certificate in the PaymentRouter and set that certificate's float cap. Both the operator and the agent authorize: enrolment attaches spend to the operator's certificate and subjects the agent to metering and to the operator's kill switch, so neither may conscript the other. A binding is permanent — an operator cannot walk an agent off a certificate whose counter is climbing.

certId.description: Certificate id to meter the agent against

floatCapUsd.description: Ceiling on the float the router will hold — what a stolen agent key can reach

tools.name: fund_float
tools.description: Move USDC into the PaymentRouter's custody, crediting the agent an equal routed balance to pay from. execute_payment tops this up on demand, so funding ahead of time is optional: float that is never idle is float that cannot be stolen.

amountUsd.description: Amount in USDC dollars to move into the router

tools.name: halt_certificate
tools.description: The operator's kill switch: stop every transfer, withdrawal and burn on a certificate. Signed by the operator, not the agent — this is the lever that exists precisely for the case where the agent's key is the problem.

tools.name: resume_certificate
tools.description: Lift an operator halt and let a certificate's payments flow again.

tools.name: quote_premium
tools.description: Price coverage: bound x duration x rate. Pass a certId to quote a published certificate from its own recorded terms, or boundUsd + durationDays to price a hypothetical one before publishing it.

certId.description: Published certificate id to price from its terms

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Read a certificate's coverage: what the operator paid, the protocol's cut, and how much of the rest the auditor has earned so far. The auditor's yield accrues in a straight line across the term, and a slash forfeits only what is still unclaimed — the premium is yield on the stake, never a second bond. Returns the quote instead when no premium has been paid yet.

certId.description: Certificate id to read coverage for

tools.name: pay_premium
tools.description: Operator buys coverage for a certificate. Payable once, and only on a VERIFIED certificate — the premium is yield on the auditor's staked capital, and there is no auditor to pay until one has attested. The protocol's share leaves in the same transaction; the rest accrues to the auditor across the term.

certId.description: Certificate id to buy coverage for

tools.name: claim_premium
tools.description: Auditor withdraws accrued-and-unclaimed yield. Allowed at any time, including mid-coverage: at every instant the accrued figure is payment for coverage already delivered. Claiming continuously converts forfeitable yield into settled income, which is deliberate — see get_coverage.

certId.description: Certificate id to claim yield from
